strengths: Comprehensive quantification of sinusoidal representation universality across models and layers with multiple validation approaches (RSA, Fourier analysis), extending prior work with concrete evidence of convergence

Methodologically important finding that probes trained on natural language contexts generalize robustly across both natural and synthetic tasks, while synthetic probes fail on natural language—challenging prior assumptions and having direct practical implications
Well-designed param-sin probe that improves on prior work by explicitly parametrizing frequency, amplitude, and phase-shift; demonstrated to outperform baselines across diverse settings

Thorough cross-layer analysis elegantly demonstrating interchangeability of representations through single-layer and leave-one-out schemes, with strong evidence of consistent encoding throughout models
Mechanistic intervention experiments (steering toward sinusoidal patterns) provide causal evidence linking representation structure to arithmetic accuracy
Effective demonstration of why general-purpose interpretability tools are inadequate for specialized data types, motivating need for tailored approaches
Solid technical execution with appropriate evaluation methodologies (RSA, Fourier analysis, linear probing, mechanistic interventions) providing triangulation of claims
weaknesses: Generalizability claims substantially overstated given limited model scope: only 3 families, maximum 15B parameters (explicitly excluding >30B), single language (English), no proprietary models tested, and Phi family showing notably weaker alignment; claim of 'almost perfect universality' not fully supported

Complete absence of multilingual or cross-linguistic-system evaluation despite acknowledging this limitation; no exploration of how findings generalize to non-English number systems (Chinese, Japanese, etc.)

Mechanistic evidence is indirect and overstated: steering corrects only 30-42% of errors, Table 2 shows 56.8% of subtraction errors have internally correct results but wrong output (indicating sinusoidality is one of multiple factors), and claims about sinusoidality 'determining' accuracy conflate correlation with causation

Critical multi-token number finding (accuracy drops to near-zero after position -1) raises severe concerns about practical applicability for real numbers but lacks deep analysis of why this occurs or how to address it

Ordinal data section (4.3) underdeveloped: uses leave-one-out on tiny datasets (7 days, 12 months), inconsistent results with older probe sometimes outperforming new approach, and acknowledged probe blind spot with zero values unresolved

Limited arithmetic scope with concerning results (division at only 5.9% accuracy in Figure 7) inadequately analyzed; no exploration of why operations differ so dramatically or investigation of complex mathematical operations

Probing interpretation gaps: linear decodability doesn't necessarily reflect true representation structure, and the inference that lower probing error indicates sinusoidality could be questioned; missing validation that probed structure is causal

Statistical rigor lacking: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars; sensitivity analysis missing for key hyperparameters (e.g., k=63 Fourier cutoff); strong claims based on point estimates
Natural language context findings under-explored: shows robustness (Figure 4) but doesn't analyze why; missing ablation studies to isolate key factors and sensitivity analysis for dataset dependence

Technical novelty is incremental: param-sin improves over prior sin probe but represents modest architectural adjustment rather than fundamental methodological advance; empirical findings extend prior work rather than introducing novel principles
